clues.title: Street sign: Street sign
text: All street name signs in Singapore follow this unique format. They are green, with rounded edges and a distinct white font.

clues.title: Road line: Road marking: HUMP AHEAD
text: Warnings are often written on the road in large letters, such as the famous “HUMP AHEAD”.

clues.title: Road line: Roadlines
text: Main roads are often divided, and commonly feature black-and-white curbs and **double yellow outside lines.**

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Stop sign: White square
text: The edge of the stop signs in Singapore has a white square outline making it unique.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vibes
text: Singapore is a highly developed city-state, characterised by an overall cleanliness and orderliness.
Main roads are often divided, and commonly feature black-and-white curbs and double yellow outside lines.
You will often see tall apartment blocks nearby.
In many cases, this “general look” is all you need to easily identify Singapore.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Sign: Road Signs
text: Road signs in Singapore are unique in that they are always set on a square white background.
Road signs in almost all other countries will not have this square background.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Buses
text: Singaporean buses are mostly lime-green, making them easily recognisable.
Other designs can also be found, for example the white-and-purple SBS Transit variants.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
